audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (sixth fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as five files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_f_<module>_N.json. Split 11 Paediatrics, 11 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 9 Psychiatry and 19 Medicine; tier mix 39 L3, 8 L4 and 3 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6742 with Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1688, Medicine on 1688 and Psychiatry on 1678. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1677 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1669, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.33 points in Paediatrics, 12.91 in Obstetrics, 12.25 in Medicine and 11.35 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 12.98, 12.50, 11.63 and 10.43 respectively, and L5 at 5.03 to 5.15 per cent in every module, a deficit of about minus 0.05 points. The strict per question argmax remains degenerate for the thirteenth consecutive fire: run literally, including the routine's 0.5 point tie break clause resolved toward the lower module total, it places all 50 questions into Paediatrics and Obstetrics and none into Psychiatry or Medicine, because the Medicine and Psychiatry L3 deficits sit 1.1 and 2.0 points behind the Paediatrics L3 leader and so never enter the near tie window. That allocation would have carried Paediatrics and Obstetrics to 1702 against 1669, a spread of 33, breaching the Section 2 module balance directive that all four modules stay within about 10 of each other, which the routine prompt itself cites as the authority for the tie break. This fire therefore used the same resolution as the previous twelve: the deficit ranking governs the weighting and the module balance cap bounds the skew, implemented as a greedy per question argmax with a guard that refuses any cell whose module total would exceed the lowest module total by more than 10. That produced 11/11/9/19 and a final spread of 10. Within each module the tier split followed the deficit ordering, which puts L3 ahead of L4 everywhere by 0.4 to 0.9 points. L5 was held at 3 questions rather than the strict zero the argmax produces, because the standing long term target is to maintain L5 at 5 per cent in each module and an all L3/L4 batch decays that share every fire; the 3 were placed in the three modules with the lowest live L5 share.
